  "reasoning": "All 16 final answers agree with the supplied worked solutions, but some source explanations contain mathematical errors. q-81506: integrating velocity gives displacement 1/2, hence position 3+1/2=7/2; the first computation line incorrectly uses 7/2 as the initial position. q-120998: displacement is (e^5-e^2)/2, giving (e^2+e^5)/2. q-81509: the triangle has area 3 and the rectangle area 6, so position is -2+9=7. q-18227 and q-73443: the depicted slopes are respectively negative on (0,2) and positive on (0,3). Their source statements that strict monotonicity implies a strictly signed derivative are false in general: a strictly monotone differentiable function can have zero derivative at isolated points. q-132666: the derivative has the sign of 4x-6, hence is negative for x<3/2. q-132667: 4x/(2x^2+1) is negative for x<0. q-48860: ln(x)+1>0 precisely when x>1/e; select the full increasing interval. q-49006: the three marked slopes are negative, positive, and zero at -2, -1, and 1 respectively. q-114698: the half-angle identity gives the antiderivative (sin(x)+x)/2+C. q-31402: substituting u=log_5(3x) gives 2 ln(5) ln|u|+C. q-73655: u=log_4(x) has bounds 1 and 2, yielding 2 ln(4) ln(2)=4(ln(2))^2; the source's first equality incorrectly changes the original x bounds from 4,16 to 2,4. q-79425: setting z=y^3 gives z'=2x(z+2), so z+2=3e^(x^2) after applying y(0)=1. The source incorrectly writes K=±e^(C1-C2): the preceding exponentiation and y>0 require K>0. q-31412: differentiating -5^(-x)/ln(5) gives 5^(-x). q-141738: only II bends upward. q-141740: I and III bend upward. These source errors do not change the selected final answers; every ma_evidence entry quotes only its owning question's supplied solution.",
